content: Constructive route: the fixed-vector hypothesis implies I-Q is injective and hence bijective on finite-dimensional R^n. Define w by (I-Q)w=u. Then Qw=w-u. Orthogonality gives w^T w=(w-u)^T(w-u), hence u^T w=1/2 because u^T u=1. Thus u^T Qw=-1/2 and HQw=Qw-2u(u^T Qw)=w. Also w is nonzero because u is nonzero. The unit-vector premise rules out n=0.
